title: Interlanguage Mathematical Translation Methodology: Slavic, Interslavic, Constructed-Language, and Terminology-Governance Notes
description:
This startup public record preserves the linguistic-methodology layer that grew out of the multilingual mathematics translation work: Ukrainian, Russian, Interslavic, constructed-language, terminology-governance, reviewer-authority, and cross-language mathematical-translation notes.

Scope. The record is intended for logbooks, terminology scaffolds, language-planning notes, reviewer-role packets, source-evidence shelves, Slavic-triangulation material, interlanguage reflections, and machine/human workflow observations. It should be cross-linked from the Emmy Noether record and the workflow/replication packet, but maintained separately because its value is partly linguistic and methodological rather than only author-specific.

Current seed payload. The initial public payload fronts a human-readable overview PDF and two compact log/method ZIPs: Noether_interlanguage_logs_quick_20260701.zip and Noether_Interlanguage_Logs_QuickFeed_20260701.zip. The current GitHub-side evidence includes the imported 2026-06-29 Slavic/interlanguage tree, the 2026-07-02 local interlanguage notes handoff, and the laptop Noether language-planning handoff mirrored through branch commit 6b983a15. The laptop handoff adds promotion-readiness, review-intake, visual-inspection, Simplified Chinese first-page triage, French missing-unit, and Arabic/Persianate source-register ledgers. These are methodology and source-evidence artifacts, not completed language editions.

Local 2026-07-02 review note. A local interlanguage_linguistics_notes_20260702 handoff package was created for human/Web review from recent Downloads material. It includes zonal/interlinguistics bot-configuration and scenario-methodology notes, but it is not automatically public-facing and should be curated or split before public promotion, especially where adult/scenario platform setup material is mixed with general interlanguage methodology.
